subtopics.title: Bond Breaking, Bond Making and the Heat of Reaction

questions.question: Forming a chemical bond always:
options: Absorbs energy in endothermic reactions only

questions.question: ΔH, the heat of reaction, is calculated as:
The sign of ΔH always describes the energy change of:
options: The system — the reacting chemicals themselves

questions.question: If bond breaking absorbs more energy than bond forming releases, then:
options: ΔH is negative and the surroundings warm
The reaction releases a surplus of heat
The products end at lower potential energy
Energy must be imported, the products sit higher, and ΔH is positive

questions.question: Which of the following is an EXOTHERMIC process?
options: The dissolution inside a cold pack

questions.question: During an endothermic reaction, the surroundings:
options: Warm up as the system releases energy
Cool down, because the system absorbs energy from them

questions.question: Photosynthesis, 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂, is endothermic because:
options: The products store more energy than the reactants, the difference being imported as sunlight

questions.question: Magnesium carbonate stops decomposing the moment heating stops because:
options: The reaction is endothermic and needs a continuous import of energy
The reaction is exothermic and overheats

subtopics.title: Activation Energy and the Activated Complex

questions.question: Activation energy is defined as:
options: The energy difference between products and reactants
The minimum energy colliding particles need in order to react
The total energy a reaction releases

questions.question: The activated complex is:
options: A stable product that can be bottled
The mixture of reactants at room temperature
The unstable transition state of maximum potential energy, with old bonds partly broken and new bonds partly formed
A compound formed between the catalyst and the products

questions.question: Paraffin and air can share a lamp for years without reacting because their combustion has:
A single match can sustain an entire fire because the match supplies:
options: All the energy the fire ever releases
A catalyst that removes the barrier
The activation energy for the first molecules, whose payout then activates the neighbours

subtopics.title: Potential Energy Graphs, Catalysed and Uncatalysed

questions.question: A graph shows reactants at 80 kJ, a peak at 170 kJ and products at 30 kJ. The forward activation energy is:
For that same graph, ΔH of the forward reaction is:
The activation energy of the REVERSE reaction on that graph is:
When a catalyst is added to this reaction:
options: Only the peak drops — reactant and product levels, and therefore ΔH, are unchanged
The product level rises to meet the lower peak
Both the peak and ΔH decrease

subtopics.title: Paying to Break, Earning to Build

questions.question: In the bucket-in-a-well picture, breaking a bond is like:
options: Winching the bucket up out of the well, which costs effort
Dropping the bucket down the well, which pays energy out

questions.question: A gas heater warms a room because:
options: Breaking the propane bonds releases heat
The new bonds in the products sit in deeper energy wells than the old bonds, and the difference is paid out as heat
Oxygen carries heat into the flame

questions.question: A cold pack chills your ankle because the dissolution inside it:
options: Costs more energy than it pays out, and bills the shortfall to the surroundings as heat
Is exothermic with a negative ΔH

subtopics.title: The Entry Fee — Why the Braai Needs a Match

questions.question: In this lesson the "entry fee" or admission price stands for:
options: The mass of wood on the braai

questions.question: After one match, a braai fire keeps itself burning because:
options: Each reaction's payout covers the admission fee for neighbouring molecules
The match continues to supply energy all evening
The activation energy vanishes at high temperature

questions.question: Wet wood struggles to burn because:
options: Water raises the activation energy of combustion
Wet wood has a positive ΔH
The early payouts are spent boiling off water instead of activating neighbouring molecules

questions.question: The size of the activation energy tells you:
options: How much total energy the reaction releases
How hard the reaction is to start — not how profitable it is overall
The final temperature of the products

subtopics.title: Reading the Hill Between Two Valleys

questions.question: On the mountain-path drawing, ΔH corresponds to:
options: The climb from the left valley to the crest
The height of the crest above sea level
The height difference between the two valley floors

questions.question: A path starting at 80, cresting at 170 and ending at 30 represents a reaction with:
Walking that same path backwards, from products to reactants, involves:
options: A climb of 90 and a finish 50 lower
No climb, because the reverse is downhill
The same climb and the same ΔH as the forward walk
A climb of 140 and a finish 50 higher than the start

questions.question: A catalyst acts like a tunnel through the ridge because it:
options: Deepens the destination valley so more energy is released
Lowers the crossing height without moving either valley — faster reaction, unchanged ΔH
Raises the starting valley to shorten the climb
